examples.en: I'm worried because I have no income these days.
My father works from dawn to make a living.

examples.ko: 이 일은 돈벌이는 괜찮지만 너무 힘들어요.
examples.en: The pay in this job is decent, but it is too hard.
He is only interested in making money.
Making money matters, but health matters more.
Work I started to earn money became a hobby.

explain: '돈벌이가 좋다', '돈벌이가 안 되다'처럼 일로 버는 수입이 얼마나 되는지 말할 때 써요. '벌이'라고 짧게도 하고, '수입'은 더 공식적인 표현이에요.

phrases.en: This job earns good money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일로 돈을 벌 수 있다는 뜻이에요. 반대는 '안 되다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the work brings in money; the opposite is 안 되다.

phrases.en: I went out to make money during vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 벌기 위해 일한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means working in order to earn money.

phrases.en: My earnings are decent these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: '돈벌이'를 짧게 줄인 말로 일상 대화에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 돈벌이, common in daily talk.

explain_en: Use it to talk about how much a job earns: '돈벌이가 좋다' (pays well), '돈벌이가 안 되다' (doesn't pay). It can be shortened to '벌이', and '수입' is the more formal word.

en: to realize; to materialize; to achieve

examples.en: I finally realized my long-held dream.
To carry out the plan, you need money and time.
Let's look for a way to make the idea real together.

examples.ko: 목표를 실현하는 데는 꾸준한 노력이 중요해요.
examples.en: Steady effort is important in achieving a goal.

examples.ko: 회사가 오랜 계획을 실현해서 새 건물을 지었어요.
examples.en: The company realized its long-held plan and built a new building.

examples.ko: 소원을 실현하고 나서 새 목표를 세웠어요.
examples.en: After my wish came true, I set a new goal.

explain: '이루다'는 꿈이나 소원에 두루 쓰고, '실현하다'는 계획, 아이디어, 정책처럼 구체적인 것을 현실로 만들 때 써요. '꿈이 실현되다'처럼 '-되다' 모양도 같이 써요.

phrases.en: My dream has finally come true.
phrases.nuance_ko: '실현하다'는 하는 사람이 주어이고, '실현되다'는 계획이나 꿈이 주어예요.
phrases.nuance_en: '실현하다' has a person as subject; '실현되다' has the plan or dream as subject.

phrases.example: 열심히 하면 이 계획을 실현할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you work hard, you can make this plan a reality.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계획이 가능한지 말할 때 '-ㄹ 수 있다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '-ㄹ 수 있다' to say whether a plan is possible.

phrases.en: I achieved my childhood dream.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이루다'는 꿈이나 소원에 두루 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '이루다' is an easier word that fits dreams and wishes broadly.

explain_en: You make a dream or goal real — neutral, written (꿈을 실현하다) '이루다' works broadly for dreams and wishes, while '실현하다' fits concrete things like plans, ideas, and policies being made real. The '-되다' form also appears, as in '꿈이 실현되다'.

t90.ax: I finally realized my long-held dream.

en: to be prevented; to be warded off

examples.en: There are many diseases you can prevent with a vaccine.

examples.ko: 운동을 꾸준히 하면 병이 예방되기도 해요.
examples.en: Exercising regularly can also prevent illness.

examples.ko: 새 규칙 덕분에 큰 사고가 예방되었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the new rule, a big accident was prevented.

examples.ko: 양치를 꼼꼼히 하면 충치가 예방되고 입 냄새도 줄어요.
examples.en: Brushing carefully prevents cavities and also reduces bad breath.

examples.ko: 미리 점검하면 고장이 예방될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Breakdowns can be prevented by checking in advance.

examples.ko: 독감은 주사로 완전히 예방되지 않지만 증상은 약해져요.
examples.en: The flu is not completely prevented by a shot, but symptoms get milder.

explain: '예방하다'는 사람이 막는 쪽이고, '예방되다'는 그 덕분에 안 좋은 일이 생기지 않은 결과를 말해요. 주어는 사람이 아니라 병, 사고, 화재 같은 일이에요. '예방 접종'도 같이 알아 두세요.

phrases.example: 손을 자주 씻으면 감기가 예방이 돼요.
phrases.en: If you wash your hands often, colds are prevented.
phrases.nuance_ko: '예방되다'와 거의 같은 뜻이고 일상 대화에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same as 예방되다 and often used in conversation.

phrases.example: 마스크를 쓰면 병을 예방할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Wearing a mask can prevent illness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 막는 쪽에서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side of the person doing the preventing.

phrases.example: 겨울이 오기 전에 독감 예방 접종을 맞았어요.
phrases.en: I got a flu shot before winter came.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병을 막으려고 맞는 주사를 말하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for the shot taken to prevent disease.

explain_en: Diseases, accidents or other problems avoided by acting in advance (감기가 예방되다) '예방하다' is the person who prevents something, while '예방되다' describes the result that a bad thing didn't happen. The subject is not a person but things like illness, accidents, or fires. Also learn '예방 접종' (preventive vaccination).

dis.h: prevented in advance; diseases, health matters
gh: blocked from happening; accidents, leaks, abuse

p.n: 방지되다 is not natural for diseases being prevented by a shot.

t90.ax: Exercising regularly can also prevent illness.

en: to be completed; to be finished

examples.en: The big file download just finished.
The construction is scheduled to be completed next month.
A text arrives right away when payment is complete.
There is homework that isn't finished yet.

examples.ko: 모든 준비가 완료돼서 이제 출발할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Everything is ready now, so we can leave.
The app got faster after the update finished.

explain: 앱, 결제, 공사처럼 정해진 일이 끝날 때 써요. '끝나다'는 일상적인 말이고, '완료되다'는 공지나 화면에서 자주 보는 격식 있는 말이에요. 앱 화면의 '완료' 버튼도 같은 말에서 나왔어요. 발음은 [왈료되다]예요.

phrases.en: The card payment is complete.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결제 화면이나 문자에서 자주 보는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen on payment screens and in text messages.

phrases.en: Open the app once the installation is complete.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앱이나 프로그램을 다 깔았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an app or program has finished installing.

phrases.en: I finished all my homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: '완료되다'보다 일상적이고 편한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More everyday and casual than 완료되다.

explain_en: Task or procedure ends with nothing left (다운로드가 완료되다) It is used when a set task such as an app process, payment, or construction finishes. 끝나다 is everyday speech, while 완료되다 is the formal word you see in notices and on screens. The 완료 button in apps comes from the same word. It is pronounced [왈료되다].

dis.h: task or procedure finished, nothing left
gh: finished as a whole product or work

p.n: 완성되다 needs something made into a whole, so it is odd for a task.

t90.ax: The big file download just finished.

examples.ko: 이번 대회의 우승자는 열두 살 아이예요.
examples.en: The winner of this contest is a twelve-year-old child.
The teacher hung a gold medal on the winner.

examples.ko: 저는 작년 우승자와 같이 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: I took a photo with last year's winner.
Nobody knows yet who the winner is.
A reporter is interviewing the marathon winner.
I learned a lot from hearing the winner's story.

explain: '우승하다'는 동사로 쓰고, '우승자'는 그 일을 한 사람이에요. 시험이나 달리기에서는 '1등'을 많이 쓰고, '우승'은 대회나 리그처럼 이름이 있는 경기에서 자주 써요.

phrases.en: Our team won the championship last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우승자가 한 일을 동사로 말한 거예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb for what a winner does.

phrases.en: The winner of the contest gets a prize.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 대회인지 앞에 붙여 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with the name of the contest placed in front.

phrases.example: 그 아이는 노래 대회의 우승자가 되었어요.
phrases.en: That child became the winner of the singing contest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과로 우승자가 되었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means someone ended up becoming the winner as a result.

explain_en: '우승하다' is the verb, and '우승자' is the person who did it. For exams or races people often say '1등' (first place); '우승' fits named contests and leagues.

examples.en: Is it okay to make a U-turn up ahead?

examples.ko: 유턴 표지판을 못 봐서 그냥 지나쳤어요.
examples.en: I missed the U-turn sign and drove right past.
U-turns are prohibited on this road.
Make the U-turn at the next intersection.
I took a wrong road, so I came back with a U-turn.
There was nowhere to make a U-turn, so I kept going straight.

explain: 운전할 때 도로에서 반대 방향으로 도는 것을 말해요. 도로 표지판에 '유턴 금지'나 '유턴 허용'이 자주 보여요. 동사로는 '유턴하다'나 '유턴을 하다'로 써요.

phrases.en: Make a U-turn at the next light.
phrases.nuance_ko: '유턴을 하다'를 한 단어로 쓴 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 유턴을 하다 in a single word.

phrases.en: U-turns are not allowed here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도로 표지판에서 자주 보는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen on road signs.

phrases.en: Please get into the U-turn lane.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유턴하려는 차가 들어가는 차선을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The lane that cars wanting to U-turn should enter.

explain_en: It refers to turning around to the opposite direction on the road while driving. Road signs often show '유턴 금지' (no U-turn) or '유턴 허용'. As a verb you say '유턴하다' or '유턴을 하다'.

examples.en: My grandmother lived a long and healthy life.
What is the secret to a long life?
This drama has run for more than ten years.
I hope my parents live a very long life.
Most people in my family have lived long.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 앞으로도 장수할 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think this shop will last a long time to come.

explain: 사람에게는 높여서 '장수하시다'로 써요. 프로그램이나 가게, 상품이 오래 이어질 때도 써요. 명사 '장수'는 '장수 비결', '장수 프로그램'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙여요.

phrases.en: My grandfather lived a long, healthy life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른에게는 높임말 '-시-'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add the honorific -시- when talking about elders.

phrases.en: The secret to long life is walking every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '장수'를 다른 말 앞에 붙여 오래 사는 방법을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 장수 placed before another noun to talk about the way to live long.

phrases.en: That show is a long-running program, on for 20 years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 아니라 프로그램이나 가게가 오래 이어질 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for shows or shops that last a long time, not just people.

explain_en: For a respected person, use the honorific '장수하시다'. It is also used for shows, shops, and products that last a long time. The noun '장수' attaches before other words, as in '장수 비결' (secret of longevity) and '장수 프로그램' (long-running show).

examples.ko: 자기 전에 적당량의 물을 마시는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's good to drink a suitable amount of water before sleeping.
Add only the right amount of salt so it isn't salty.
Please take the medicine in the proper amount.
The right amount differs a little from person to person.
The recipe just says 'right amount', so I'm confused.

examples.ko: 비료를 적당량 뿌려 주면 화초가 잘 자라요.
examples.en: If you sprinkle the right amount of fertilizer, plants grow well.

explain: '적당히'는 부사라서 '적당히 넣다'처럼 쓰고, '적당량'은 '적당량을 넣다'처럼 명사로 써요. 레시피에 '소금 적당량'이라고 적혀 있으면 정해진 숫자 없이 맛을 보며 넣으라는 안내예요. '알맞은 양'으로 풀어 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: Add an appropriate amount of salt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 레시피에서 양을 정하지 않고 맛을 보며 넣으라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: In recipes it means to add by taste, with no fixed amount.

phrases.en: Take just the right amount and eat it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '적당량'을 쉬운 말로 풀어서 쓴 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier way to say '적당량' in plain words.

phrases.en: It's best to eat only a moderate amount of snacks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 너무 많지 않게 알맞은 양만 먹으라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means to eat only a fitting amount, not too much.
phrases.en_equiv: to eat only the right amount

explain_en: '적당히' is an adverb, as in '적당히 넣다', while '적당량' is a noun, as in '적당량을 넣다'. If a recipe says '소금 적당량', there is no fixed number, so you add salt while tasting. It can also be spelled out as '알맞은 양'.

examples.en: Early-morning movies have cheaper tickets.
I watched a movie at the early showing on the weekend.
I like the early showing because there are few people.
Shall we go to the early showing tomorrow morning?
My friend likes the early showing too.
The early showing is the most comfortable for me.

explain: '조조할인'이라는 말로 아주 자주 나와요. 일반적인 시간 표현이라기보다 영화관에서 쓰는 말에 가까워요. 영화와 상관없이 이른 시간은 '이른 아침'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Watching a movie with the early-bird discount is cheaper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이른 시간 영화를 싸게 보는 일을 말해요. 가장 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The cheap price for early movie shows; the most common usage.

phrases.en: I woke up in the morning and watched an early show.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이른 아침 시간의 영화를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a movie in the early morning slot.

phrases.example: 그 영화는 주말에 조조로 볼 거예요.
phrases.en: I'll watch that movie in the early show this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '로'를 붙여 언제 볼지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '로' says which showing you'll watch.

explain_en: It shows up most often in '조조할인' (early-bird discount). It is more of a movie-theater word than a general time expression. An early morning in general is '이른 아침'.

en: express bus; nonstop bus; direct bus

examples.en: I took an express bus from Seoul to Busan.
The express bus hardly stops on the way.
Please check the express bus timetable.

examples.ko: 이 직행버스는 한 시간에 한 대 있어요.
examples.en: This express bus runs once an hour.
It takes about two hours by express bus.
The express bus is a bit more expensive than a regular bus.

explain: 서는 곳이 많은 '완행'과 대비해서 써요. 터미널에서는 '직행으로 한 장 주세요'처럼 줄여서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.example: 부산 가는 직행으로 한 장 주세요.
phrases.en: One ticket for the express to Busan, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 터미널에서 '직행버스'를 줄여 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form used at the terminal.

phrases.en: I wanted to get there fast, so I took the express bus.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직행버스를 이용할 때 가장 기본으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic phrase for riding an express bus.

phrases.en: I checked the express bus timetable on the internet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 출발 시간을 알아볼 때 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when looking up departure times.

explain_en: Bus that goes to the destination without stopping on the way. It contrasts with '완행', which stops at many places. At a terminal people often shorten it, saying '직행으로 한 장 주세요' (One express ticket, please).

t90.ax: This express bus runs once an hour.

examples.en: At a construction site, you must wear a hard hat.
Please wear a mask when you enter the hospital.

examples.ko: 자동차를 탈 때는 안전벨트를 착용해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to wear a seat belt when riding in a car.
At the pool, wearing a swim cap is the rule.

examples.ko: 시험 중에 시계를 착용한 사람은 없었어요.
examples.en: Nobody wore a watch during the exam.
If you don't wear a helmet, you pay a fine.

explain: '입다, 쓰다, 끼다, 신다'는 물건마다 달라지지만 '착용하다'는 옷, 모자, 마스크, 안전 장비를 한 단어로 말해요. 안내문과 규칙에 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '입다', '쓰다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Please put on your seat belt before boarding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 방송에서 부탁할 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common way to politely ask people in signs and announcements.

phrases.en: That player is wearing a helmet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 몸에 걸치고 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something currently being worn.

phrases.en: I wear thick clothes in winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 옷에는 '입다'를 쓰고, '착용하다'는 규칙이나 안내문에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily talk use '입다' for clothes; '착용하다' fits rules and notices.

explain_en: Formal; any item, in rules and notices. '입다', '쓰다', '끼다', and '신다' change with the item, but '착용하다' covers clothes, hats, masks, and safety gear in one word. It shows up in notices and rules, while everyday talk uses '입다' or '쓰다'.

p.n: The clothing verb only works for clothes.

t90.ax: Nobody wore a watch during the exam.

examples.en: The tire was flat, so I went to the car repair shop.
I got the engine oil changed at the garage.

examples.ko: 이 근처에 믿을 만한 카센터가 있어요?
examples.en: Is there a trustworthy car repair shop near here?

examples.ko: 카센터 사장님이 차를 꼼꼼히 봐 주셨어요.
examples.en: The owner of the repair shop checked my car carefully.
The garage is closed on Sundays.

examples.ko: 차에서 이상한 소리가 나서 카센터로 가져갔어요.
examples.en: The car was making a strange noise, so I took it to the garage.

explain: 자동차를 고치거나 점검하는 가게를 말하는 한국식 영어예요. 영어권에서는 'car center'가 아니라 'repair shop'이나 'garage'라고 해요. 비슷한 말로 '정비소'가 있어요.

phrases.en: I had the brakes fixed at the repair shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: '카센터'와 비슷한 뜻이고 조금 더 공식적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 'car center' but a bit more formal.

phrases.en: The owner of the car center explained kindly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게 주인을 부를 때 '사장님'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 'sajangnim' to refer to the shop owner.

phrases.en: I got my car repaired at the car center.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차를 고친 장소를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say where the car was repaired.
phrases.en_equiv: to repair at the car center

explain_en: This is Korean-style English for a shop that repairs or inspects cars. In English-speaking countries people say 'repair shop' or 'garage', not 'car center'. A similar Korean word is '정비소'.

t90.ax: The garage is closed on Sundays.

examples.en: The train passes through the tunnel.
I passed the document screening.

examples.ko: 검사대를 통과하면 비행기를 탈 수 있어요.
examples.en: After going through the checkpoint, you can board the plane.
This bill will pass the National Assembly.

examples.ko: 시험을 통과한 사람은 다음 주에 와요.
examples.en: People who passed the test come next week.
It was hard to get through the narrow door.

explain: 장소를 지나갈 때도, 시험이나 심사를 넘길 때도 써요. 시험에서 점수를 받아 붙는 것은 '합격하다'를 더 자주 말하고, 서류나 심사에는 '통과하다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I passed the baggage check at the airport.
phrases.nuance_ko: 검사나 심사를 문제없이 넘겼다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you got through a check or review without problems.

phrases.en: I passed the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점수를 받는 시험에는 '통과하다'보다 '합격하다'를 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For score-based exams, '합격하다' is more common than '통과하다'.

phrases.en: Unfortunately, I did not pass the interview.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 못하다'로 넘기려 했지만 안 됐다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you tried to get through but did not.

explain_en: Go through a place, or pass an exam or inspection. It works both for passing through a place and for getting past an exam or screening. For passing an exam by score, '합격하다' is more common, while '통과하다' suits document reviews and screenings.

dis.h: go through; also pass a test
gh: travel along a road; traffic use

p.n: 통행하다 does not suit a tunnel crossing; it means traveling along a road.

examples.en: My back hurt, so I saw a traditional Korean medicine doctor.

examples.ko: 한의사는 맥을 짚고 몸 상태를 살펴봤어요.
examples.en: The doctor took my pulse and checked my condition.
My aunt works as a traditional Korean medicine doctor.
The doctor gave me acupuncture.
I asked the doctor about teas that are good for the body.
A traditional Korean medicine doctor is also a medical professional who sees patients.

explain: 병원에서 진료하는 사람은 '의사', 한의원에서 진료하는 사람은 '한의사'라고 해요. 한의사가 일하는 곳은 '한의원'이에요.

phrases.en: I went to the Korean medicine clinic yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한의사가 일하는 곳이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The place where a doctor of Korean medicine works.

phrases.en: The Korean medicine doctor prepared medicine for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 부르거나 높여 말할 때 '선생님'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '선생님' when addressing or showing respect.

phrases.en: My dream is to become a doctor of Korean medicine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about dreams or careers.
phrases.en_equiv: to become a Korean medicine doctor

explain_en: A doctor at a hospital is an '의사', while one at a traditional Korean clinic is a '한의사'. The place where a 한의사 works is a '한의원'.
